good: Right shape and proportions: rounded lid, skull plaque, chunky feet.

off: The carved detail is smeared into soft blobs at this size.
It is a print-style solid block, so the lid does not open.
One plain wood colour, with no metal bands or gold.

good: One tidy piece, nothing broken to repair.
off: Plain milky grey stands in for glass, so it needs a real glass look.
The cork or cap was not included, only the bottle.

good: The retro look is readable from a distance.
off: It is a thin printed shell with open edges, and shrinking it folded the sheets into a crumpled mess.
Too heavy for a small prop even after the damage.
Needs to be rebuilt from its outline instead of cleaned up.

good: The cleanest result of the set: crisp, light and the right height.
Stands on the ground with its base at the middle.
off: Metal and lamp glass share one dark colour.
Very tall and thin, so players could walk into it from odd angles.

good: Tray and lid are kept as two separate named parts.
off: The lid and tray were printed side by side, and my guess at putting the lid on leaves it floating above the rim.
Edges are jagged after shrinking.
Rebuilding this crate would be quicker than fixing it.

good: Already light, so nothing was lost.
Planks and crossed legs are right, at a sensible full size.
off: Flat brown wood colour, with no grain or wear yet.

good: Clear bench shape with proper slats.
A huge scan-like source was brought down to a light model.
off: The usual shrinking got stuck on this messy mesh, so it was rebuilt from a rough shell and the edges are softer than the original.

good: Already light, so it was kept almost as it came.
off: It is a tiny island scene, not just a tower; the rock base would have to go to use the building alone.

good: Body and wheels are two separate named parts.

off: It is a toy-style tractor: a boxy cab with no seat or engine detail.

good: Cute, soft, relaxed creature that suits a storybook look.

off: Plain clay colour, with no comb or beak colours yet.
